label: Rømmegrøt
step: sour, cook with flour, skim the butterfat
note: Eaten at feasts, with sugar, cinnamon and the skimmed fat poured over; cured meats and flatbread on the side. The skimmed fat is served on the side as the butter.

about.text: A thick Norwegian porridge of soured cream, whole milk and wheat flour, eaten with sugar and cinnamon on festive occasions.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Cooking the rømme with flour breaks the cream emulsion: the butterfat rises and is lifted off. The porridge underneath is thick and sweetish.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: Rømme is cooked with some of the flour until the fat starts to separate.

steps.name: stir in
steps.note: The rest of the flour and the milk are added gradually.

steps.name: skim
steps.note: The fat is skimmed off and served warm on the side.
